claim: *Probability in the software factory.* Engineers encode consequential intent; agents fulfill the encoded obligations. The two probability terms condition on representation R, omitted for legibility. The encoded property also defines the acceptable region for realizations, allowing independent evidence to inform admission or rejection.
topology: Engineering intent → Encoded property → Fabricator → Realization. Separate brackets identify P(E) correct encoding and P(F|E) fulfillment of encoded obligations. Encoded property also points downward to supply tolerance; realization points downward for measurement. A candidate inside the acceptable subset leads to admitted change; a candidate outside leads to revise/reject. No measurement or acceptance arrow returns to the fabricator.
required_terms: tests, PBT, analysis, simulation, human judgment
bw_encoding: Light gray identifies the encoded property and the acceptable subset it defines. The containing Possible realizations region and ordinary production/output nodes remain white. No broad outer factory enclosure or decorative header boxes.
redesign: Author-reference redraw separates correct encoding from fulfillment of encoded obligations while showing the encoded property also supplying the tolerance used to evaluate realizations. The lower region is correctly named Possible realizations, not a single proposed change. Its acceptable subset contains several possible realizations; one outside point illustrates revision/rejection. Bare hierarchy labels retain the established book style.
alt: A software factory production process goes from engineering intent to encoded property to fabricator to realization. P(E) denotes correct encoding, and P(F|E) denotes fulfillment of encoded obligations. Engineers authorize intent; agents interpret, implement, and correct. The encoded property also supplies tolerance, while tests, property-based testing, analysis, simulation, and human judgment measure the realization. The lower Possible realizations space contains a smaller Acceptable region with several points and one point outside. Within-tolerance realizations lead to admitted change; outside-tolerance realizations lead to revise or reject.
